task_description: Build a Node.js HTTP service that supports user registration, password sign-in, short-lived access tokens, rotating refresh tokens, protected profile access, and sign-out. Store users and sessions in an in-memory repository, reject revoked or reused refresh tokens, validate request bodies, and return consistent JSON errors. Include middleware that authenticates protected requests and configuration for token lifetimes and signing secrets.

Build a Node.js service for a multi-tenant document workspace with user sign-in and role-based authorization. Define owner, editor, and viewer permissions, enforce tenant isolation on every document operation, provide endpoints to invite members and change roles, and return appropriate authorization errors. Use an in-memory repository, centralized authentication and authorization middleware, request validation, and audit records for membership changes.

Build a Node.js web service with cookie-based authenticated sessions. Implement sign-in, sign-out, session renewal, concurrent-session listing and revocation, idle and absolute expiration, and protection for a state-changing account endpoint. Use secure cookie attributes, server-side session storage, request validation, and consistent handling for missing, expired, or revoked sessions. Keep the session store in memory so the behavior is easy to exercise locally.

Build a Node.js account-verification service that adds time-based one-time-code verification after password sign-in. Support enrollment, code challenge and verification, limited clock skew, single-use codes, recovery-code consumption, lockout after repeated failures, and authenticated device listing and revocation. Store test users and verification state in memory, keep secrets out of responses and logs, validate all inputs, and expose JSON endpoints with clear error status codes.

Build a Node.js API authentication service for machine clients. Allow administrators to create, list, rotate, revoke, and expire API credentials with named scopes and per-client quotas. Require credentials for protected endpoints, enforce scope checks, prevent revoked credentials from being accepted, redact secrets from logs and responses, and record an audit trail. Use an in-memory store, configurable quota windows, input validation, and consistent JSON error responses.

Build a Node.js service that manages a catalog of books in a relational database. Provide create, retrieve, update, delete, and paginated list operations with author filtering. Include connection pooling, migration configuration, parameterized queries, request validation, and a transaction that updates a book and records an audit entry atomically. Return consistent JSON errors and close database resources cleanly during shutdown.

Build a Node.js reservation service backed by a relational database. Expose endpoints to create, view, cancel, and list reservations for limited-capacity rooms. Prevent overbooking under concurrent requests using an appropriate transaction and locking strategy, enforce time-range and ownership validation, support idempotent reservation requests, and return meaningful conflict errors. Include connection lifecycle handling and a small migration or schema definition for local setup.

Build a Node.js order service using a document-oriented database. Store customers, orders, and line items with schema validation, useful indexes, and optimistic concurrency for order updates. Provide endpoints to create an order, retrieve it, change its status, and list orders by customer and date range. Validate totals and state transitions, handle duplicate requests safely, and return consistent JSON errors with clean connection shutdown behavior.

Build a Node.js service that imports product updates and exposes searchable product data from a relational database. Accept a batch of records, validate each record, report row-level failures, and apply valid changes in a transaction with an import summary. Provide filtered and paginated reads, enforce unique product identifiers, use parameterized database operations, and make a failed batch safe to retry without leaving partial updates.

Build a Node.js idempotency service backed by a key-value data store with expiration support. Accept requests containing an idempotency key, return the original result for a repeated completed request, coordinate concurrent requests using an in-progress state, and release or expire abandoned work safely. Add an HTTP endpoint for inspecting non-sensitive status, configurable retention, input validation, and clear behavior for conflicting request bodies.

Build a Node.js HTTP service that accepts one CSV upload of customer records, validates file size and headers, streams rows without loading the entire file into memory, normalizes valid records, and writes them to a JSON Lines output file. Return accepted and rejected counts, provide a downloadable rejection report with row-level messages, and safely clean up temporary files after processing.

Build a Node.js service that receives PDF invoices and extracts a defined set of fields including invoice number, date, supplier, line items, and total. Validate required fields and numeric consistency, classify documents with extraction errors, store normalized results as JSON, and expose an endpoint for retrieving the result and an error report. Process uploads through temporary files, enforce size limits, and remove temporary artifacts after completion.

Build a Node.js XML feed processor for product catalog updates. Accept an uploaded XML document, parse namespaced product and inventory elements, validate required fields and numeric values, transform valid entries into normalized JSON, and produce a structured report for rejected entries. Reject malformed documents safely, prevent external resource resolution, enforce upload limits, and make the processed result available through a JSON endpoint.

Build a Node.js service that imports a spreadsheet workbook containing monthly sales sheets and exports a normalized report. Validate required sheet names and columns, handle dates and numeric cells consistently, aggregate totals by product and month, report invalid rows without discarding valid data, and generate a downloadable tabular summary. Support bounded upload sizes, temporary-file cleanup, and clear JSON status and error responses.

Build a Node.js archive-processing service that accepts an archive of images and metadata files, validates the archive manifest, extracts only permitted file types into a temporary workspace, transforms metadata into a single JSON document, and returns a processing summary. Defend against path traversal, duplicate names, excessive entry counts, and decompression-size limits. Clean up temporary content on success and failure and expose a downloadable validation report.

Build a versioned Node.js REST API for support tickets. Provide endpoints to create, retrieve, list with cursor pagination and status filtering, update status, add comments, and delete tickets. Validate path parameters and request bodies, return appropriate HTTP status codes, implement centralized error handling, and expose a machine-readable API description endpoint. Use an in-memory store and keep response shapes consistent across success and error cases.

Build a Node.js multipart media-upload API for user profile images. Accept one upload with a configurable size limit, validate content type and dimensions, create a normalized stored representation, expose metadata and download endpoints, and support replacement and deletion. Return clear validation errors, avoid trusting client filenames, prevent path traversal, and clean up temporary files when processing fails. Keep storage local to the disposable application workspace.

Build a Node.js real-time collaboration API using WebSocket connections. Allow clients to join a named workspace, broadcast edits to other members, acknowledge message sequence numbers, reconnect after temporary disconnects, and receive a bounded recent-event history. Validate message shapes, isolate workspaces, remove disconnected clients, limit message size, and expose an HTTP health endpoint. Use an in-memory event store and document the client message protocol.

Build a Node.js search API over a simulated asynchronous product source. Provide validated query, sort, filter, and cursor-pagination parameters; enforce per-client rate limits with retry guidance; return stable pagination results; and expose an endpoint showing non-sensitive rate-limit status. Handle upstream failures consistently, prevent unbounded query sizes, and include correlation identifiers in responses. Keep the upstream source local and deterministic for development.

Build a Node.js webhook ingestion API for payment-like event notifications from a simulated sender. Verify signed request payloads, reject stale timestamps and replayed event identifiers, process each event idempotently, expose event status and retry history, and return response codes that distinguish accepted, duplicate, and invalid deliveries. Store events and processing state in memory, redact sensitive fields from logs, validate payloads, and provide a local endpoint for inspecting sanitized results.

Build a Node.js credential service for user passwords. Implement registration, password verification, password change, and account lockout with a memory-backed repository. Use a well-established password hashing approach with per-password salts and configurable work parameters, never return or log password material, validate credentials without revealing account existence, and provide consistent authentication errors. Include a safe configuration path for upgrading work parameters when users next authenticate.

Build a Node.js service for encrypted application secrets with authenticated encryption. Accept a server key through configuration, generate a unique nonce for every record, store only ciphertext and required encryption metadata in memory, and expose create, retrieve, rotate, and delete endpoints. Support key-version rotation without exposing plaintext, validate requests, redact errors and logs, and reject records whose authentication tag or key version cannot be verified.

Build a Node.js document-signing service that creates and verifies digital signatures for canonical JSON documents. Provide endpoints to sign a document, retrieve public verification material, and verify a submitted document and signature. Define deterministic canonicalization, include key identifiers and signature metadata, reject altered or malformed inputs, support key rotation while retaining verification of old signatures, and ensure private key material never appears in responses or logs.

Build a Node.js service that derives encryption keys for user-owned notes from a passphrase and a stored salt. Use a recognized password-based key-derivation approach with configurable cost parameters, encrypt and decrypt note content with authenticated encryption, support changing the passphrase by re-encrypting notes, and reject tampered records. Store salts, ciphertext, nonces, and versioned parameters but never plaintext or passphrases; validate inputs and return non-sensitive errors.

Build a Node.js comment API that accepts user-authored rich text and returns safely rendered content. Define an explicit allowed formatting policy, sanitize untrusted markup and links, reject unsafe schemes and dangerous attributes, preserve plain text meaning, and validate request size and structure. Add security headers, consistent errors, and tests or examples covering scripts, event-handler attributes, malformed markup, and encoded input without implementing a custom parser or cryptographic primitive.

Build a Node.js HTTP service that emits structured application logs for each request and important domain operation. Include correlation identifiers, method, route, status, duration, severity, and safely redacted selected headers and fields. Support configurable log levels, consistent JSON serialization, an error boundary that records useful context without secrets, and a health endpoint that reports logging configuration without exposing credentials.

Build a Node.js service that writes structured application events to rotating local log files. Support size- or time-based rotation, configurable retention, startup recovery when an old file is present, graceful shutdown, and a simple endpoint for listing available log metadata without serving secrets. Ensure concurrent writes remain ordered per process, handle write failures explicitly, and redact authorization values and configured sensitive fields before serialization.

Build a Node.js product-details service with a bounded in-process cache. Add configurable TTL and maximum entries, cache hit and miss statistics, explicit invalidation, stale-while-revalidate behavior, and protection against duplicate upstream requests for concurrent misses. Use a simulated asynchronous upstream source, expose cache health metrics, and log cache outcomes and failures with correlation identifiers and redaction.

Build a Node.js session-summary service using a shared key-value cache. Implement namespaced keys, TTL refresh for active sessions, bounded payload sizes, cache invalidation on sign-out, and a safe fallback when the cache is unavailable. Prevent stale writes from replacing newer values, expose non-sensitive cache health information, and produce structured logs for hits, misses, fallbacks, and invalidations with request correlation identifiers.

Build a Node.js HTTP gateway that records request traces across a simulated chain of two asynchronous upstream services. Create trace and span identifiers, record start time, duration, status, and redacted attributes, propagate context between local calls, support configurable sampling, and export completed traces to a local JSON Lines sink. Handle partial upstream failures, bound retained trace data, and expose an endpoint with aggregate tracing health statistics.
